plainLanguage.toggleTooltip: Swap jargon for plain wording — technical terms stay available on hover and in the Theory-tab glossary
plainLanguage.glossaryIntro: Every term this mode rewrites, with its plain equivalent and the technical meaning behind it.

prefill.long: Prefill — the parallel pass where the model ingests every prompt token at once and builds the KV cache. Sets TTFT.

decode.plain: writing one word piece at a time
decode.long: Decode — autoregressive generation: one token per step, with every step re-reading the model weights and KV cache from VRAM.

ttft.plain: wait before the first word appears
ttft.long: TTFT (Time To First Token) — how long from sending your prompt until the first output token shows up. Set by prefill speed.

tpot.plain: time to write each following word piece
tpot.long: TPOT (Time Per Output Token) — average time to generate each token after the first. Set by decode speed.

gemm.long: GEMM (matrix-matrix multiplication) — many multiply-accumulate operations executed at once. High arithmetic intensity, so it is compute-bound; prefill is dominated by it.

gemv.long: GEMV (matrix-vector multiplication) — one row of math per token whose speed is capped by memory bandwidth; decode is dominated by it.

kvCache.plain: notes on everything read so far
kvCache.long: KV cache — per-token Key/Value vectors kept in VRAM so already-processed tokens don't have to be recomputed. Grows linearly with context length.

prefixCaching.long: Prefix caching — reusing the KV cache of a shared prompt prefix across requests or turns instead of recomputing it from scratch.

vram.long: VRAM — the memory on the graphics card that holds model weights, the KV cache and activation buffers.

token.long: Token — the chunk of text (~¾ of a word) that a model reads and writes; prompts and outputs are counted in tokens.

computeBound.long: Compute-bound — the math units (tensor cores / FLOPs), not memory, set the pace. Prefill usually is compute-bound.

bandwidthBound.long: Bandwidth-bound — moving weights and cache from VRAM is the bottleneck, not math. Decode usually is bandwidth-bound.
